title: Dev Duel
description: DevDuel is a six-round competitive coding challenge designed to help students improve their programming, problem-solving, coding speed, and competitive programming skills. The event follows a weekly challenge format, with coding challenges conducted every Saturday and Monday at 8:00 PM, followed by evaluation and a verified leaderboard release every Wednesday. Since many participants are beginners, the questions will be beginner-friendly and moderately challenging, allowing participants to understand and solve problems while developing their coding skills.
fullDescription:
DevDuel is a structured competitive coding event designed to provide students with regular coding practice in a competitive yet beginner-friendly environment. The event focuses on improving programming fundamentals, logical thinking, problem-solving ability, coding speed, and accuracy while preparing students for technical placements, hackathons, and competitive programming.
The event consists of six rounds, beginning on 29 August 2026 and progressing through a combination of normal and elimination rounds. Rounds 1, 2, 3 and 5 are normal rounds, Round 4 is an elimination round, and Round 6 is the final elimination round scheduled for 3 October 2026. final_repot.pdf
Each normal round contains two coding challenges. The first challenge is conducted every Saturday at 8:00 PM, followed by evaluation on Sunday. The second challenge is conducted every Monday at 8:00 PM, followed by evaluation on Tuesday. On Wednesday, the scores from both challenges are verified and the official leaderboard is released. final_repot.pdf

title: DUOS DASH 4.0
description: Duos Dash 4.0, organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter during UTSAV 2026, was an exciting team event designed for pairs. It featured four engaging rounds that tested communication, creativity, and quick thinking. The first round, Bomb Diffusion, involved one teammate guiding the other to defuse a virtual bomb in Roblox, emphasizing coordination and trust. Fliptionary challenged participants with drawing on a flipped screen while their partner guessed the word, leading to fun and confusion. In Emoji Enigma, teams acted out movie names represented through emojis from different languages. The final round, Draw & Dare, used UNO cards to assign creative tasks, giving teams chances to earn points. Overall, the event blended technology, fun, and teamwork, perfectly matching the vibrant spirit of UTSAV
fullDescription:
Duos Dash 4.0 is a four-round interactive team competition that tests communication, coordination, creativity, reflexes, and spontaneity. Teams of two compete across dynamic mini-games, and winners are decided based on cumulative points. Round 1 – Bomb Defusal (Roblox): One participant views the virtual bomb while the other holds the manual. Using verbal communication only, they must solve modules within the time limit. Round 2 – Fliptionary: One participant draws a word using an inverted setup while the teammate guesses. Points are awarded based on correct guesses. Round 3 – Draw & Dare: Teams pick UNO cards that assign different types of dares (action, verbal, expressive, challenge). Points are awarded for successful completion. Round 4 – Emoji Enigma: Teams decode emoji combinations representing movies and cultural elements. Points are given for speed and accuracy. The team with the highest total score wins.
KEY OUTCOMES :
All the participants left the event with a feeling of
accomplishment after playing the games. They were all highly anticipating the results. These games fostered a sense of connection and strengthened the bond present between two friends. It also strengthened the teamwork and initiative of the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter beyond technical activities since
we learnt what it is like to function as a group and complete our tasks.

title: Grandmaster's Gambit 4.0
description: Grandmaster’s Gambit 4.0 is a fast-paced, team-based chess event that blends classic gameplay with strategic twists and quick-thinking challenges. Teams of two compete across multiple stages, starting with rapid mini-games, followed by intense best-of-three matches, and ending in high-pressure knockout rounds played on dual boards. With a mix of traditional chess, unique variants, and time-bound puzzles, the event tests not just skill, but adaptability, coordination, and decision-making under pressure.
fullDescription:
The event commenced with Mini Game 1 – Roots & Routes, wherein teams engaged in a decryption-based puzzle to discover a concealed chess artifact, assessing their speed and pattern recognition abilities.

Subsequently, the Qualification Round was conducted in a best-of-3 format, comprising two standard chess games (rapid/blitz) and a final game featuring a modified chess variant with unique piece functionalities, demanding both skill and adaptability.

Following this, Mini Game 2 – Legends of the Board presented teams with interactive chess puzzles, requiring the execution of precise checkmate sequences, thereby evaluating their calculation and accuracy under time constraints.

Based on overall performance, teams progressed to the Knockout Stage, where the top 14 teams participated in a Swiss-format round, with the top 6 teams qualifying. These teams then engaged in a round-robin semifinal, ensuring each team competed against all others. Finally, the top 2 teams advanced to the finals, contested in a best-of-3 format, where consistency and teamwork determined the ultimate victor.

title: VAULT OF TRIALS 2.0
description:
Vault of Trials 2.0 is an interactive, logic-based game that tests critical thinking and problem-solving through a structured, timed challenge.
Teams enter the game via a custom-built website and have 1 hour to progress through three levels (A, B, C), each containing multiple locked doors. Every door presents questions from domains like mathematics, English, and logical reasoning. Players must choose the correct path by solving these challenges, with difficulty increasing at each level.
Unlocking the correct final door leads to a coding-decoding puzzle that determines the winner. Points are awarded at each stage, with penalties for repeated wrong answers, making both accuracy and strategy important. The game blends logic, speed, and decision-making in a competitive format.
fullDescription:
The VAULT OF TRAILS 2.0, a sequel to the original VAULT OF TRIALS,  was a creatively designed logic testing event which was implemented in the form of an engaging game. The website of the game was customized and curated by our skilled technical team.  
The event began with the explanation of rules and regulations as well as the structure of the game, following which the participants entered their team names to start the game which they accessed through a link. The teams were provided a built-in timer of 1 hour, after which the game closes itself. There were three levels to the game- A, B, C. Each door of these levels was locked by riddles and questions varying for different domains like mathematics, reasoning or English. The objective of the game was to lead on the correct path and find the correct door at the earliest. The first question was an easy math problem following which the storyline of the game was displayed. Next was level A of the game where participants encountered 3 locked doors which were opened by answering the mathematical logic problem given on the door. Each level A door opened into 3 more level B doors which were locked with an English-based riddle on them. Each level B door opened into 3 doors of level C, which were locked with a logical reasoning-based question. The level C doors were particularly harder to solve in comparison to level A and B and tested the critical thinking of the participants. The game was so designed that upon unlocking the correct level C door, a last hard question based on coding-decoding algorithm was presented. Solving this last riddle was the game winning move. 
Unlocking the initial door awarded teams with 2 points and 1,2 and 3 points for doors A, B and C respectively and a point is deducted for answering 3 questions incorrectly. Scoring was crucial in case no team was able to reach the final door. Therefore, for the tie-breaker, the teams with the highest score would be declared as the winner. 
Overall, the game, Vault of Trials 2.0 tested participants' critical and analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities through a fun and exciting game.
location: AI-DS Data Science Laboratory, 6th Floor, PJA Block

title: Operation Black Veil
description: A beginner friendly cybersecurity Capture The Flag (CTF) event where participants solved real world inspired challenges involving digital forensics, cryptography, and web investigation.

Participants worked in teams of two and progressed through chapter based challenges, each representing a stage in a cyber investigation.

As participants advanced, the difficulty increased, requiring them to decode messages, recognize patterns, and apply logical reasoning. The final stage required participants to combine all gathered insights to reach the solution, with winners determined based on accuracy and speed. The event successfully enhanced analytical thinking, problem solving skills, and interest in cybersecurity.

title: Bulls, Bears and Breakouts
description: An interactive trading simulation where participants managed virtual hedge funds, responding to AI-generated market events in real-time.
fullDescription: Bulls, Bears and Breakouts was conducted as an interactive trading simulation where participants formed teams and acted as virtual hedge funds. Each team utilized a trading dashboard displaying price charts and market indicators for corn futures and options. Instead of coding strategies, participants guided their trading decisions by adjusting predefined parameters such as risk levels, stop-loss, trade frequency, and entry thresholds. Simulation Dynamics: Market Events: AI-generated events including policy announcements, weather update_strs, supply shocks, and volatility changes were introduced at the start of each round. Real-time Adaptation: These events influenced price movements, requiring teams to analyze impacts and modify their strategy parameters in real-time . Evaluation Criteria: Team performance was evaluated based on their final portfolio value, effectiveness of risk management, and overall adaptability to market fluctuations. Collaboration: The competitive format emphasized quick thinking and internal team coordination to navigate the dynamic trading environment.
outcomes: The event successfully promoted critical thinking and collaboration while providing a practical understanding of how market conditions and risk management influence financial outcomes[cite: 25]. Participants gained useful insights into strategic decision-making and built confidence in navigating fast-moving trading scenarios.
location: CSE UG Lab 03, 2nd Floor, Platinum Jubilee Academic Block

title: ACM ROCS 2025
description: The two-day ACM ROCS (Research Opportunities in Computer Science), hosted by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter and ACM India, featured nine distinguished speakers from institutions like Google, IBM, IISc, and TCS, covering cutting-edge research in AI, Generative Modeling, Cryptography, and more.
fullDescription: The ACM ROCS (Research Opportunities in Computer Science) event was held on September 26th and 27th, 2025, hosted by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter in collaboration with the ACM India. The event was supported by RNSIT and GAT ACM Student Chapters as community partners and Unibic as the snacks partner. The two-day program featured nine distinguished speakers from Google, IBM, IISc, and TCS.   🗓️ Day 1: September 26th   Inauguration: The event commenced with the traditional lamp lighting, presided over by Dr. Seemanthini K (Faculty Sponsor) and Dr. Gowrishankar (Faculty Advisor).  Overview of ACM India & Career Insights: Prof. Jayant Haritsa (Former President of ACM India Council) provided an overview of ACM India's role and highlighted career progression opportunities and various programs.  Virtual Session on ROCS and Research Careers: Venkatesh Raman (Professor at IMSc) introduced ROCS's inception, objectives, and discussed the importance of pursuing a research career.  Talk on Database Systems: Prof. Jayant Haritsa (IISc) described database systems as the hidden power behind modern computing, covering relational DBMS fundamentals, query processing, and the ACM SIGMOD 2026 conference.   Talk on IBM Research: Prof. Padmanabha V. Seshadhri (IBM Research India) discussed the work at IRL, the evolution of foundation models, Granite language models, and the WATSONX platform, concluding with internship opportunities.  Opportunities on Edge Accelerators for AI Workloads: Dr. Yogesh Simmhan (IISc Bangalore) discussed the hybrid cloud, the edge-cloud continuum, the importance of edge accelerators, and open research questions in systems research.   Ask Me Anything Session: An interactive Q&A was held with Prof. Yogesh Simmhan, Prof. Meenakshi D'Souza, and Dr. Karthikeyan Shanmugam, focusing on research and career choices.  Talk on Software Testing: Prof. Meenakshi D'Souza (President of ACM India) highlighted the importance and cost of software testing, covering black-box and white-box testing, research directions, and career opportunities.  Multimodal Earable Devices for Longitudinal Monitoring: Jayavardhana Gubbi (Principal Scientist at TCS Research) discussed innovations in wearable technologies, focusing on EarEEG systems and multimodality in earable devices.  Overview of Generative Modeling Research: Dr. Karthikeyan Shanmugam (Google DeepMind India) presented research on generative modeling, introducing the Matryoshka model and transformer that power Gemma 3N, and explored non-autoregressive approaches for text and image generation.   🗓️ Day 2: September 27th   A Cryptographer's Dilemma: Bhavana Kanukurthi (Associate Professor at IISc Bangalore) explored cryptography from the perspective of rational behavior, discussing auctions, the prisoner's dilemma, and rational multiparty computation (MPC).  Algorithms for Assembling Genomes: Chirag Jain (Assistant Professor at IISc Bangalore) provided an overview of genome assembly challenges, highlighting concepts like overlap graphs and the advantages of repeat-aware fragmentation.  Algorithmic Game Theory: Siddharth Barman (Associate Professor at IISc Bangalore) delivered a talk on game theory fundamentals, including Sperner's lemma, and discussed applications in economic policies and decision-making, such as Nash social welfare.  Final Ask Me Anything Session: Siddharth Barman, Bhavana Kanukurthi, and Chirag Jain addressed questions on research, career options, and academic challenges.  Closing: Dr. Seemanthini K. Gowda delivered closing remarks, expressing gratitude to the attendees, faculty, and partners.
outcomes: ACM ROCS provided a valuable platform for students, faculty, and industry experts to engage with cutting-edge research and emerging technologies. The event successfully reinforced the importance of research and collaboration, leaving participants motivated for future academic and professional pursuits.

title: Fun with Algorithms
description: An engaging workshop, led by Mr. Sachin Lodha (Chief Scientist, TCS Research), connecting theoretical algorithms to real-life problem-solving and decision-making under uncertainty.
fullDescription: The 'Fun with Algorithms' workshop, led by Mr. Sachin Lodha, Chief Scientist at TCS Research, successfully connected theoretical algorithms with relatable, real-life problem-solving. The session started by comparing an algorithm to a 'good recipe', a systematic, quick process that solves a problem in a limited number of steps.    Key Concepts and Problems Discussed:   Hamlet’s Ski Rental Problem: This classic scenario introduced the concept of online algorithms and making optimal decisions under uncertainty (deciding whether to rent or buy skis daily without knowing the total duration).   Treasure Hunt Problem: This challenge involved a blindfolded person finding a treasure on the X-axis with the least walking. This demonstrated the doubling strategy and key ideas like competitive ratio and the Beeza-Yates theorem (a core principle in competitive analysis).  The workshop's objectives were achieved through engaging storytelling and practical examples, successfully sparking interest in algorithm design and competitive programming.
outcomes: The workshop provided participants with a clear understanding of algorithms and how to apply them to real-life problems. Participants learned practical strategies, such as the Doubling Strategy, and key ideas like online algorithms, competitive ratio, and cost optimization, fostering logical thinking and an interest in competitive programming.

title: ESP: CryptoVerse
description: An online talk by Mr. Sikhar Patranabis (Staff Research Scientist, IBM Research India) on the challenges of transforming theoretical cryptographic security into real-world applications, focusing on Zero Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs).
fullDescription: The Eminent Speaker Talk, 'CryptoVerse: Securing The Digital World,' was conducted online by Mr. Sikhar Patranabis, Staff Research Scientist at IBM Research India. The talk focused on bridging the gap between provable cryptographic security and real-world deployment against modern cyber threats. The central topic was Zero Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), a cryptographic protocol allowing a prover to convince a verifier that a statement is true without revealing any information beyond the truth of the statement. ZKPs were explained via four core principles: completeness, soundness, zero knowledge, and succinctness, using intuitive examples like the color blindness test and the Ali Baba cave scenario. The session also detailed ZKPs of knowledge, the use of arithmetic circuits for complex relations, and modern protocols like SNARKs. Practical applications in blockchain technology, particularly zk-rollups, were highlighted for improving scalability and reducing gas fees.
outcomes: Participants gained valuable insights into applying theoretical cryptographic concepts to real-world systems, enhancing their understanding of advanced security protocols and encouraging exploration of research opportunities in cryptography and blockchain scalability.

fullDescription: The BMSCE ACM Student Chapter initiated its community service journey with SAMANVAYA #1 on March 13, 2025. The event, themed 'Together for Change,' focused on providing lunch for 72 children at Amrutha Shishu Nivasa in Bengaluru. A total donation of ₹2,000 was made, comprising ₹1,000 from member contributions (14 donors) and ₹1,000 from the chapter’s treasury. Five members visited the orphanage to deliver the donation and spend time with the children. This initiative marked the beginning of the club’s commitment to community welfare, reinforcing the belief that collective efforts can create a lasting impact.
outcomes: The event successfully encouraged social responsibility and community engagement among members, fostered a sense of empathy, strengthened teamwork, and set a precedent for future community service initiatives under the SAMANVAYA series.

title: CS Pathshala
description: A community service and technical education initiative, in collaboration with the BMSCE Rotaract Club, focused on introducing computational thinking concepts to school students through grade-specific, hands-on activities.
fullDescription: The CS Pathshala program by the ACM India Council was integrated into the iTeach initiative by the BMSCE Rotaract Club, held at Vidya Vinayaka Samsthe, Bengaluru. The partnership introduced computational thinking through dynamic, grade-specific activities emphasizing problem-solving, logical reasoning, and teamwork.   Activities by Grade:   Grades 1 & 2: Focused on Pattern Parade (sequencing/categorization) and Sorting Station (logical thinking).  Grades 3 & 4: Focused on Step-by-Step Instructions, Loops, and Decision-Making using a Battleship-style game and flowchart logic.  Grades 5 & 6: Focused on Problem Decomposition and Data Representation via a Treasure Hunt using coordinates and riddles.  Grade 7: Focused on Advanced Algorithms and Programming Concepts by having students write, test, and debug algorithms for creating a paper airplane, and using real-life scenarios to create decision trees (if-else conditions).
outcomes: The event successfully introduced computational thinking to young learners, fostering critical thinking and problem-solving skills among students, while volunteers honed essential skills like communication and teamwork.

title: ACM India Chapter Summit 2024
description: A three-day national summit hosted by BMSCE and RVCE, uniting ACM Chapters across India to explore the theme of "Sustainable Computing" and foster collaboration.
fullDescription: The ACM India Chapter Summit 2024 was a three-day national event (Dec 19-21) hosted by B.M.S. College of Engineering (BMSCE) and R.V. College of Engineering (RVCE), centered on the theme 'Sustainable Computing.' The summit united ACM Student Chapters, Professional Chapters, and SIG Chapters from all over India, focusing on community building and societal contributions. The commitment to sustainability was visible in all aspects, from eco-friendly materials used for merchandise to plastic-free banners.   Key Highlights:   Day 0 (Dec 19): Included participant check-ins, an address by Ms. Maria Dsouza Choudhary on the ACM Ambassador Program, and the networking activity 'Duos Dash,' concluding with a welcome dinner.  Day 1 (Dec 20): Featured an Indian cultural welcome dance by BMSCE Paramvah, a talk by Dr. Meenakshi D’Souza (President, ACM India), and a keynote by Dr. Rama Govindaraju (NVIDIA) on 'Sustainable AI.' Award-winning chapters presented their best practices. The afternoon included a session at RVCE on 'Technology for Sustainability' and a poster competition on 'Imagining India in 2030 (SDG).'  Day 2 (Dec 21): Featured keynotes on 'Online Education in the NEP Era' (Prof. Andrew Thangaraj, IIT Madras), 'Democratizing Data and Responsible AI' (Prof. Manish Parashar, University of Utah), and 'Technology for Social Good' (Raghu Dharmaraju, ARTPARK at IISc). Participants engaged in regional brainstorming sessions and peer group presentations to develop action plans for the upcoming year, with winners receiving ABF funding.   Key Achievements:   Seamless collaboration between BMSCE and RVCE.  Inspired innovative discussions on Sustainable Computing.  Fostered collaboration among 87 ACM Chapters across India.
outcomes: The summit successfully showcased technology's vital role in sustainability, encouraged innovative ideas and practical solutions, and created a collaborative space for knowledge-sharing and networking among students, faculty, and industry leaders.

title: Flag Heist 2.0
description: A time-bound, competitive event centered on capturing multiple bases via Google Forms, testing participants' mathematical, visualization, and problem-solving skills.
fullDescription: FLAG HEIST 2.0, conducted by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter on the occasion of Phase Shift 2024, challenged participants to capture multiple bases within a time limit of one hour and fifteen minutes. Bases were represented by Google Forms containing a series of questions across diverse categories, including tech-based, coding-based, Phase Shift theme-based, logical reasoning, quantitative analysis, mini-games, riddles, and case-study tech-based problems. Teams had to answer all questions correctly in a form to capture a base; even one wrong answer invalidated the capture. Points were awarded based on speed of submission: the first team to capture a base won a blue flag (50 points), the second won a pink flag (30 points), and subsequent captures won yellow flags (10 points). The event took place from 10 am to 1 pm in the CSBS Lab, PJA Block.
outcomes: The event successfully created an engaging and competitive atmosphere, promoting critical thinking, collaboration, and healthy competition. Participants had a chance to showcase their skills and expand their knowledge base.

title: Web Wars 2.0
description: A 3-day frontend web development competition during Phaseshift 2024, challenging participants to design sustainability-focused web solutions using modern frameworks.
fullDescription: Web Wars 2.0 was a 3-day tech adventure organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter as part of the technical fest, PhaseShift 2024, themed 'Resurgence.' The competition challenged 37 participants (in teams of 2) to craft sustainability-focused websites. The event was held in CR1, 7th Floor, AIML Dept, PJ Block, and featured Mr. Deepak Chawla, Co-Founder of HiDevs, as a resource person.   Day 0 (Dec 3): Theme Unveiling, focused on 'Resurgence' sub-themes like Green Tech, Eco-friendly Agriculture, and Sustainable Fashion.  Day 1 (Dec 4): Four challenges were introduced, including designing a Navigation Bar, integrating Multimedia/Social Media, implementing a Dark Mode Toggle, and a Surprise Challenge: Carbon Footprint Calculator.  Day 2 (Dec 5): The final day involved offline website presentations and evaluation, followed by judge guidance. Allowed technologies included HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript, React.js, Vue.js, Angular, SASS/LESS, WebGL, Bootstrap, and Tailwind CSS. The event successfully fostered creativity and skill enhancement.
outcomes: All participating teams successfully demonstrated their innovation and creativity skills. The event provided valuable skill enhancement and exposure to participants, concluding successfully with a competitive and enjoyable spirit.

title: ACM Nexus
description: A lively and engaging orientation meet organized to introduce new members to the club's activities, roles, and details of the ACM India Chapter Summit 2024.
fullDescription: ACM Nexus was a lively and engaging meet for new and existing members of the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter, held on November 22, 2024, from 4 PM to 6 PM in Audi 2 (PJA Block). The event began with a welcome by Srikanth, followed by Roshini discussing the club's recent and upcoming events. Kanishka provided a clear understanding of the various club roles and behind-the-scenes operations, including marketing, design, logistics, and sponsorship. Bhuvan then gave a detailed presentation on the ACM India Chapter Summit 2024, covering logistics, accommodation, tentative schedule, and introducing speakers. The atmosphere was kept fun and interactive with a quick game and a dedicated games session hosted by Indraneel and Devaj. The event concluded with a thank-you note by Hrithik and a group photo.
outcomes: ACM Nexus successfully connected members, clarified the different roles within the club, and provided detailed updates on future events, including the planning and logistics of the ACM India Chapter Summit 2024. The event left attendees feeling more involved and updated.

title: Clock of Confusion
description: A fun and challenging event featuring a series of games designed to test participants' memory, riddle-solving, critical thinking, and teamwork skills.
fullDescription: The 'Clock of Confusion' event, organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter in collaboration with BMSCE IEEE Student Branch, was a fun and challenging event held on November 15, 2024 (2:00 pm to 4:00 pm) in PJ Block, 5th floor, classrooms 504 and 505. The event featured a series of engaging games for 23 teams (46 participants) designed to test critical thinking, teamwork, and strategy:    Puzzle Game: Fastest team to solve a scrambled puzzle with a reference image earned the most points.   Card Game: Teams arranged a scrambled deck of cards (1 to 10) in ascending order in the shortest time, restarting if they picked the wrong card.   Memory Game: Teams observed a table of objects for one minute and answered questions based on memory.   Trading Game: Teams traded random items to accumulate the most valuable combination, testing negotiation skills.   Mystery Box Conundrum: Teams strategically decided when to open boxes containing clues or challenges to manage their points.   The team with the highest score at the end of all rounds was declared the winner, emphasizing the importance of strategy and quick decision-making.
outcomes: Clock of Confusion provided an excellent opportunity for participants to solve riddles in a new way, enhance teamwork, and practice creative thinking in a supportive and engaging environment. The varied rounds ensured that each team member could contribute their strengths, promoting a collaborative spirit.

title: AI Frontiers Workshop
description: A 6-day comprehensive workshop and 36-hour hackathon focused on Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
fullDescription: The 'AI Frontiers' workshop, conducted in collaboration with Hi-Devs, was a comprehensive 6-day event held primarily at the PJA Block, 7th floor, AIML Seminar Hall. The workshop aimed to equip 82 participants with foundational and advanced knowledge in Generative AI, LLMs, and RAG.    Days 1 & 2 (Nov 14-15): Focused on theoretical foundations, real-life applications, LLM types, token limits, and vector databases.   Day 3 (Nov 16): A hands-on coding session where participants implemented Generative AI using LangChain and LLMs.   Days 4 & 5 (Nov 17-18): A continuous 36-hour online hackathon involving 16-17 teams (2-4 members each) solving innovative problem statements related to Generative AI and RAG, avoiding reliance on conversational AI tools.   Day 6 (Nov 19): Project demos, presentations, and the announcement of winners. Prizes included ₹3,000 (1st), ₹2,000 (2nd), and ₹1,000 (3rd).   The event successfully blended theory, practice, and competition, creating a holistic learning experience.
outcomes: The workshop secured 82 registrations, providing practical exposure that enhanced participants' problem-solving and collaborative skills. Eight attendees successfully secured internships with Hi-Devs, and the event fostered significant awareness of the transformative potential of Generative AI and RAG

title: Jumble Jam 2.0
description: A fun-infused technical event consisting of three rounds designed to foster teamwork, creativity, and problem-solving skills among participants.
fullDescription: The 'Jumble Jam 2.0' competition, organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter in collaboration with BMSCE IEEE WIE, was a fun and challenging event held on October 28, 2024 (11:00 am to 1:00 pm). The event, held in the PJA Block, 6th floor, Computer Science Data Science Lab, was designed to test knowledge, technical skills, and teamwork among 27 teams (54 participants) through three rounds:    Round 1: Quiz Round - Teams of two answered 20 on-screen questions to test general knowledge.   Round 2: Tech and Fun - Teammates split roles; one solved technical questions while the other played online games. Performance in this round earned letters.   Round 3: Unscramble - Teams reunited to use their earned letters to collaboratively unscramble a 9-letter word, relying on logical deduction.   The team with the highest score across all rounds was declared the winner. The event successfully promoted critical thinking, collaboration, and competitive spirit.
outcomes: Jumble Jam 2.0 provided an excellent opportunity for participants to practice problem-solving, teamwork, and creative thinking in an engaging environment. The varied rounds ensured that each team member could contribute their strengths, promoting a collaborative spirit among participants.

title: The Art of Encryption
description: An online poster design competition held during Cybersecurity Month with the theme "Secure Our World," aiming to raise awareness about digital safety.
fullDescription: The Art of Encryption was a poster-making competition held online throughout October 2024 by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter to observe Cybersecurity Month. The theme was 'Secure Our World,' encouraging students to use a creative outlet to depict various cybersecurity concepts and raise digital safety awareness. Participants were given one month to design and submit their posters to a specified email, adhering to guidelines regarding format, size, and the inclusion of the BMSCE and BMSCE ACM Student Chapter logos. The posters were judged based on their relevance to the theme, creativity, quality of design, and clarity of message. The two best posters were selected, and the winners received a total prize pool of ₹1500/-.
outcomes: The event achieved tremendous success with 27 total participants. It provided a platform for participants to showcase their poster-making skills and creativity, successfully increasing awareness among them about the importance of cybersecurity and digital safety.

title: Game Theory Showdown
description: An intellectually stimulating event focused on strategic thinking and decision-making, featuring classic and complex game theory-based challenges.
fullDescription: The Game Theory Showdown, an intellectually stimulating event, engaged 25 participants in strategic thinking and decision-making through three challenging rounds. The event, hosted at PJ Block CR 507, aimed to test strategic thinking and decision-making skills in a fun and competitive environment, focusing on the application of game theory.   Round 1: Featured classic games like 'Matching Pennies' and 'Dynamic Rock-Paper-Scissors-Lizard-Spock (RPSLS) with Cards,' introducing mixed strategies and Nash Equilibrium. Round 2:Advanced to more complex scenarios with 'Sealed Bid Auctions' and 'Bertrand Competition,' emphasizing strategic bidding, pricing, and balancing competition with profit maximization.  Final Round:Culminated in the intense 'Prisoner's Dilemma,' which tested participants' ability to build trust and strategize whether to cooperate or betray without knowing the other's choice.   Participants showcased their logical reasoning, strategic planning, and adaptability, leaving with a deeper understanding of game theory principles.
outcomes: The event successfully enhanced participants' understanding of game theory concepts, fostered a spirit of healthy competition, and provided a platform for the practical application of strategic thinking, resulting in improved logical reasoning, strategic planning, and adaptability.

title: Byte Battle
description: A multi-round coding competition and quiz event aimed at fostering teamwork, enhancing coding skills, and promoting competitive programming among students.
fullDescription: The Byte Battle competition, organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter, was a well-planned event held on June 20, 2024, in the PG Block, 2nd floor, Computer Lab, from 2:00 pm to 4:00 pm. The event promoted teamwork and coding skills among 17 teams (51 participants total). The competition consisted of multiple rounds:   Byte Battle Challenge: Teams of three worked together, with each member solving one coding problem, testing problem-solving and collaboration.  * Watts of Wisdom Round:A quiz segment on technological innovation and the future of electrification, testing broader technological understanding.  Advanced Code Relay Challenge: Teams tackled more difficult coding problems by taking turns coding in short intervals, emphasizing adaptability and seamless collaboration under pressure.   Overall, the dynamic and engaging event provided a valuable opportunity for participants to sharpen their coding skills, learn new strategies, and work effectively in teams.
outcomes: The Byte Battle provided participants with an excellent opportunity to enhance their coding skills, collaborate effectively in teams, and develop strategic thinking. The competitive environment and structured challenges prepared participants for real-world coding tasks and competitive programming events.

title: CTRL+ALT+CREATE
description: A four-round web design and coding competition focused on enhancing skills in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a theme of Electric Vehicles (EVs).
fullDescription: The CTRL+ALT+CREATE web design challenge, hosted by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter in collaboration with IEEE PES and SENSORS COUNCIL, aimed to enhance participants' skills in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Held offline on 14th June 2024, the competition challenged teams of two to create static web pages based on the theme of Electric Vehicles (EVs) for PES Day. The event was structured into four rounds (from 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM), each with specific tasks, time limits, and points weighting. Tasks included designing a sticky navigation bar, implementing image and text transitions, creating accordion menus, and developing detailed footer sections. Participants were evaluated on creativity, adherence to guidelines, and the functionality of their designs. The team with the highest points at the end was declared the winner. The event successfully fostered technical proficiency, teamwork, and innovation.
outcomes: CTRL+ALT+CREATE was highly successful, showcasing participants' enhanced proficiency in web development fundamentals, creativity in design, and problem-solving abilities under time constraints. The event also fostered teamwork and collaboration among students interested in web design.

title: InnoVision
description: An insightful seminar on process and prototype design, featuring Mr. Nithin Ravi, focusing on real-world applications and startup case studies.
fullDescription: The BMSCE ACM Student Chapter organized the InnoVision seminar on process and prototype design, featuring Mr. Nithin Ravi, an MBA candidate from ISB with substantial startup experience. Held in the ISE Seminar Hall, the session began with Mr. Ravi sharing his entrepreneurial background and insights into startup challenges. The core discussion utilized case studies of successful startups like Blinkit and Zepto to illustrate key principles of process design, emphasizing the importance of identifying and meeting the target audience's needs. Participants then engaged in a hands-on activity centered around a hypothetical startup called 'Fit Raho' (functional training). The task involved creating a complete process design to launch the offering and acquire the first 500 paid members for a new fitness center in Bangalore. This exercise required developing strategies for target audience, segmentation, targeting, positioning (STP), pricing, promotion, and location preferences. The combination of theoretical knowledge, practical case studies, and collaborative problem-solving made the seminar an informative and highly engaging experience.
outcomes: The seminar fostered an engaging and collaborative environment, enhancing participants' problem-solving skills and their ability to devise effective business strategies for process and prototype design.

title: Cipher Quest
description: A cryptography and puzzle-solving event where 30 teams decoded encrypted messages and solved intricate challenges to save their homeland.
fullDescription: The CIPHER QUEST event, organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter, was held on Sunday, 19th May 2024, at MEL LAB 2. The event challenged 30 teams (two participants each) to decode encrypted messages contained within password-protected zip files. Teams earned 50 points per successfully unlocked folder by deciphering various types of codes. Additionally, they were required to demonstrate typing accuracy by blind typing sentences after each successful decipher. The elimination rounds involved decoding messages using different cipher techniques, testing cryptographic skills, teamwork, and communication under pressure. The teams with the fastest and most accurate decoding and typing advanced to the final round. The final round featured a unique game called Cryptic Ludo, which used two dice and allowed teams to use basic mathematical operations on the numbers rolled for strategy. Progressing through each quarter of the board required solving additional puzzles like Sudoku, crosswords, and mazes. Four teams reached the final showdown, demonstrating exceptional problem-solving, teamwork, and strategic thinking.
outcomes: The event successfully enhanced participants’ teamwork, problem-solving skills, and ability to think strategically and quickly under pressure.

title: Grandmaster's Gambit 2.0
description: A chess variant competition organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter in collaboration with Videsh Educon.
fullDescription: The GRANDMASTER’S GAMBIT 2.0, organized by the BMSCE ACM Student Chapter in collaboration with Videsh Educon, was a day-long competition focused on various chess variants, held on Friday, 17th May 2024, at the AIML Lab 1. The event ran from 9:00 AM to 3:30 PM. Initial rounds featured six pools, each with four to five teams, playing 4-player chess variants (4P, Chaturaji, and 4P Giveaway). The top two teams from each pool advanced. Round 2 introduced 2-player variations, including 'fog of war,' Atomic, Giveaway, and Crazy House. The semifinals were a round-robin format for the top teams, featuring unique variations like the XXL Variant (expanded chessboard) and Bughouse (simultaneous play on two adjacent boards with piece passing). A sudden-death 1v1 game served as the tie-breaker. The thrilling finals were a standard 4-player game, with the winning team receiving ₹2500 and the runners-up receiving ₹1500. The event successfully fostered connections and reinforced the love for chess among participants.",     "outcomes": "The competition successfully showcased strategic prowess and sportsmanship, providing participants with valuable experiences and reinforcing the enduring appeal of chess.
outcomes: The competition successfully showcased strategic prowess and sportsmanship, providing participants with valuable experiences and reinforcing the enduring appeal of chess.

title: Duo’s Dash 2.0
description: As part of utsav24 BMSCE ACM Student Chapter had organized DUO’s DASH 2.0 which was a series of mini-games with a fun twist.
fullDescription: Duo's Dash, a unique event designed to test teamwork and interdependence, saw an enthusiastic participation of 100 individuals paired into dynamic duos. Conducted on the 2nd floor common area of the PJ block, the event featured four innovative mini-games that challenged participants to race against the clock while demonstrating their cooperative skills. The atmosphere was charged with excitement and anticipation as teams navigated through a blend of AI-driven and traditional game modes, vying for the title of the most reciprocal and dynamic duo.  The event kicked off with  "Inverted Pictionary, " where one teammate drew a word on an inverted laptop screen, and the other guessed the object. This game tested not only their artistic skills but also their ability to synchronize hand and brain movements under pressure.  In  "Movie Charades using AI, " participants described movie scenes to an AI generator, which created images for their teammates to guess. This game highlighted the intersection of technology and creativity, pushing participants to think quickly and communicate effectively.   "Bomb Defuse " added a layer of tension, as duos had to verbally collaborate to defuse a virtual bomb in a Roblox game, with one holding the bomb and the other the manual. The intensity of this game required precise communication and trust, as any misstep could lead to a virtual explosion.  Finally,  "Snake and Ladder " combined elements of chance and skill, as rolling dice led participants to perform fun activities, earning points for their teams. Each activity required participants to think on their feet and adapt quickly, adding to the overall excitement of the event.  As the day concluded, Duo's Dash celebrated the resilience and cooperation of its participants, with the undefeated pair against the clock emerging victorious. The event was praised for its innovative integration of AI and traditional gaming elements, providing a thrilling yet challenging experience. Participants shared their positive feedback, applauding the event's creativity and the seamless execution of the mini-games. Duo's Dash not only fostered teamwork and patience but also showcased the potential of AI in enhancing interactive and engaging activities, making it a memorable event for all involved.
outcomes: Overall it was a fun and engaging game, an all-round experience involving thrill,team-work and skill

title: GRE-Demystified
description: The objective of the GRE Exam Preparation Webinar was to equip prospective test-takers with comprehensive strategies and practical insights to excel in the GRE, enhancing their readiness for graduate admissions.
fullDescription: The GRE Exam Preparation Webinar, held online and led by Rohan Lakhne, was a highly anticipated event that drew the attention of 65 prospective GRE test-takers. With over a decade of experience in training students for GRE, GMAT, and SAT exams, Rohan Lakhne, the Head of Learning and Development at AECC, brought invaluable insights and practical knowledge to the session. His expertise and interactive teaching style kept the audience engaged throughout the two-hour seminar, providing a comprehensive overview of the GRE exam structure and its significance in graduate admissions. The webinar was meticulously structured to cover all critical aspects of the GRE exam, beginning with an introduction to the test's format and importance. Each exam section was explored in depth: Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning, and Analytical Writing. Rohan shared effective strategies for tackling reading comprehension, text completion, and sentence equivalence in the Verbal section. In Quantitative Reasoning, participants learned techniques for problem-solving, data interpretation, and quantitative comparisons. The Analytical Writing segment focused on crafting compelling essays, providing participants with tips to excel in both issue and argument tasks. Additionally, Rohan discussed time management techniques, study schedules, and the importance of practice tests, which are crucial for efficient preparation. The seminar concluded with an interactive Q&A session, allowing participants to address their specific queries and concerns. This personalized interaction was highly appreciated, as reflected in the positive feedback from attendees. Participants praised the comprehensive coverage of exam topics and the practical, actionable advice provided by Rohan. The certification process, which granted certificates of attendance to all participants, added a formal acknowledgment of their commitment to preparation. Overall, the GRE Exam Preparation Webinar successfully equipped attendees with the essential strategies and insights needed to excel in the GRE, underscoring the value of expert guidance in achieving their academic goals.
outcomes: The seminar provided participants with a solid understanding of the GRE exam structure and effective strategies for each section. Attendees gained practical problem-solving skills and techniques to manage their study schedules and test anxiety.

title: CareerCraft
description: This workshop aimed to give insights about interview preparation and internship opportunities
fullDescription: The workshop on interview preparation, networking, personal branding, and finding the right internship opportunity was meticulously curated by Ms. Madhura Kawadiwale, an esteemed interview preparation coach and soft-skills trainer, held from 6:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. With a wealth of experience in talent development, Ms. Madhura delved into comprehensive strategies tailored to elevate participants' career prospects. The session commenced with a deep dive into interview preparation, encompassing techniques to articulate strengths, handle behavioral questions, and demonstrate alignment with organizational values. Participants gained invaluable insights into crafting compelling resumes, optimizing LinkedIn profiles for professional networking, and leveraging social media platforms to enhance personal branding. Throughout the workshop, Ms. Madhura seamlessly integrated practical exercises and role-playing scenarios, enabling participants to refine their communication skills, build confidence, and project a strong professional image. Discussions on effective networking strategies, including informational interviews and leveraging alumni networks, empowered participants to expand their professional connections and access hidden job markets. Furthermore, Ms. Madhura provided guidance on cultivating a distinctive personal brand, emphasizing authenticity, consistency, and storytelling to resonate with potential employers and stakeholders. As the session concluded, Ms. Madhura underscored the importance of continuous learning and self-improvement in navigating today's dynamic job market. Participants left the workshop equipped with actionable strategies, renewed confidence, and a clear roadmap to pursue internship opportunities aligned with their career aspirations. The event's success was attributed to Ms. Madhura's expertise, engaging delivery style, and the collaborative efforts of the organizing team, ensuring a transformative learning experience for all attendees.
outcomes: The workshop provided invaluable insights into interview preparation, networking, and personal branding. Participants gained practical strategies and renewed confidence to navigate the job market effectively. Ms. Madhura's expertise and engaging teaching style ensured a transformative learning experience for all attendees

title: Mastering DSA
description: This workshop aimed to provide insights into fundamental data structures, algorithm design, and their applications.
fullDescription: The Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) course, starting on January 21, spans over three months and is meticulously designed for beginners aiming to excel in technical interviews. Conducted online, this comprehensive program offers a robust curriculum covering essential concepts in Java and C++. With a registration fee of ₹300, participants are provided with a thorough grounding in DSA, guided by expert instructor Abhinav Kumar from Skylark Drones. His extensive experience in data structures and algorithms ensures that learners receive top-notch education and practical insights. Sudeep and Harsha, as event coordinators, have played pivotal roles in orchestrating this course, seamlessly ensuring its success. Each week of the course delves into specific topics, beginning with foundational concepts such as Time Complexity, Pointers, and Searching Techniques. As the course progresses, participants explore a variety of critical subjects including Arrays, Strings, Sorting Techniques, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, Recursion, and Trees. Advanced topics such as Heap Tree, Hashing, Graphs, Dynamic Programming, Greedy Algorithms, Backtracking, and Bit Manipulation are also comprehensively covered. The final weeks include mock interviews and reviews, ensuring that participants are well-prepared for real-world technical challenges. The teaching methodology employed in the course is highly interactive and practical. Weekly lectures are designed to be comprehensive, fostering an engaging learning environment. Hands-on coding problems and practical exercises help reinforce theoretical knowledge. Participants have access to valuable resources including lecture notes, reference guides, and practice problems, enhancing their learning experience. Weekly Q&A sessions provide an opportunity for interactive discussions, allowing learners to clarify doubts and deepen their understanding. The positive feedback from participants highlights the effectiveness of this approach, appreciating the course structure and the instructor’s expertise.
